 Sri. Keshava.K., B.A., Ll.B.,

Chief Judicial Magistrate,
 Bengaluru.

Dated this 05th day of November, 2025
 C.C.No.4214 of 2019
Complainant : State by the Police Sub Inspector,
 Nandini Layout police station,
 Bengaluru.

[By Assistant Public Prosecutor]
 - Vs - Accused no. 1) Thimmegowda,
 S/o.Late.Chikkanna,
 Aged about 47 years,
 2) Smt.Lakshmamma,
 W/o.late.Chikkanna,
 Aged about 65 years  3) Narasamma,
 W/o.Late.Krishnappa,
 Aged about 47 years,
 4) Manjunatha,
 S/o.late.Krishnappa,
 Aged about 28 years,
 2  C.C.4214/2019  Accused no.1 to 4 are R/at.No.9,
 13th main, Sakkama Badavane,
 Nandini Layout, Bengaluru.
(Case against accused no.5-Sarojamma is  split up and registered in C.C.9756/2022)

Prema vs Thimmegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153369637/
1  [By B.K.Ramesh...
Advocate]
JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Nandini Layout police station against the accused no.1 to 5 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
324, 504 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 and C.W.1 are husband and wife and their marriage was solemnized about 20 years back and were residing at the matrimonial house at Sakkamma Badavane, after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention, used to instigate the accused no.1 and the accused no.1 was ill treating the C.W.1 for petty reasons, picked up quarrel with her and drove her out of the matrimonial home along with her son ie C.W.2 and did not look after the family needs.

Further on 02.05.2018 at about 10.00A.M when the C.W.1 to 3 met the accused no.1 to 5 at Spandana Hospital, Nandini Layout and were discussing about the act of accused no.1 of driving out C.W.1 and 2 out of matrimonial home, the accused picked up quarrel with C.W.1, abused her in filthy language, assaulted C.W.1 to 3 with hands and iron rod, helmet and caused simple bleeding injuries and therefore the C.W.1 C.C.4214/2019 lodged the complaint against the accused no.1 to 5 before the Nandini Layout Police seeking necessary action against the accused persons.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.217/2018 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.
Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused no.1 to 5 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.
4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, the accused no.1 to 4 appeared before the court and were enlarged on bail, the accused no.5 remained absent, as such case against accused no.5 was ordered to be split up and separate split up case has been registered in C.C. 9756/2022.
Meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused no.1 to 4 ,
therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused no.1 to 4 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried,
accordingly proceeded with trial against the accused no.1 to Prema vs Thimmegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153369637/
2 4.
5.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution has got examined two witnesses who are said to be the complainant and eye witness as P.W.1 C.C.4214/2019 and 2 and and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and P.2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused no.1 to 4 , as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-3 to 8 are ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned APP.

Consequently,
statement of accused U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C is recorded.
6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond was obtained from the accused no.1 to 4 .

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.
Whether

the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 and C.W.1 are husband and wife and their marriage was solemnized about 20 years back and were residing at the matrimonial house at Sakkamma Badavane, after marriage while C.W.1 was residing with the accused no.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention, used to instigate the accused no.1 and the accused no.1 was ill treating the C.W.1 for petty reasons,
picked up quarrel with her and drove her out of the matrimonial home along with her son ie C.W.2 and did not look after the family needs and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence of "subjecting C.W.1 to cruelty " punishable under section 498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 02.05.2018 at about 10.00A.M when the C.W.1 to 3 met the accused no.1 to 4 along with accused no.5 (against whom split up case is registered) at Spandana Hospital, Nandini Layout and were discussing about the C.C.4214/2019 act of accused no.1 of driving out C.W.1 and 2 out of matrimonial home, the accused picked up quarrel with C.W.1, abused her in filthy language and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence of "intentional insult"
punishable under section 504 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above mentioned date, time and place the accused no.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of that common intention, without any provocation assaulted C.W.1 to 3 with iron rod and caused simple bleeding injury and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence of "voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous means" punishable under section 324 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?

Prema vs Thimmegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153369637/
3 4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above mentioned date, time and place the accused no.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of that common intention, without any provocation assaulted C.W.1 to 3 with hands and caused simple hurt and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence of "voluntarily causing hurt" punishable under section 323 r/w Sec.34 of IPC ?
5.What Order?

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 to 4 : In the 'Negative'
 Point No.54 : As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 4 :These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.

10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has got examined two C.C.4214/2019 witnesses who are said to be the complainant and injured as P.W.1 and 2 and and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and P.2.

As far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence available on hand the C.W.1/P.W.1- Prema in her evidence deposed that accused no.1 is her husband, accused no.2 to 4 are the relatives of accused no.1 and P.W.1 intially supported the case of prosecution and deposed that the accused no.1 to 4 used to instigate the accused no.1 and the accused no.1 was ill treating the C.W.1 for petty reasons, picked up quarrel with her and drove her out of the matrimonial home along with her son ie C.W.2 and did not look after the family needs.

Further on 02.05.2018 at about 10.00A.M when the C.W.1 to 3 met the accused no.1 to 5 at Spandana Hospital, Nandini Layout and were discussing about the act of accused no.1 of driving out C.W.1 and 2 out of matrimonial home,
the accused picked up quarrel with C.W.1, abused her in filthy language, assaulted C.W.1 to 3 with hands and iron rod, helmet and caused simple bleeding injuries.
Further P.W.1 deposed that she lodged complaint as per Ex.P.1 and police came to the spot and drew spot mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
Initially PW1 supported the case of prosecution and counsel for accused no.1 to 4 cross examined the witnesses at length.

During her cross examination, PW1 being the prime witnesses turned fully hostile to the case of the prosecution in the lengthy cross-examination made by learned counsel for accused no.1 to 4 and she admitted the suggestion that the accused no.1 to 4 are the relatives of accused no.1 and she does not know the contents of complaint which is marked as Ex.P.1, the accused did not pick up quarrel with her and she further deposed that she has compromised the matter with the accused.
11.

The son of C.W.1 ie C.W.2 is examined as P.W.2, P.W.2 in his C.C.4214/2019 evidence deposed that accused no.1 is his father and other accused are the relatives of accused no.1, he further deposed that the accused did not physically and mentally harass C.W.1 and did not quarrel with them, did not assault them and did not cause injuries to them.
Further he deposed that he has not seen the iron rod and helmet pertaining to this case.

Prema vs Thimmegowda on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153369637/
4 12.

As the complainant/P.W.1 and P.W.2 injured being the material witnesses in this case have not supported the case of the prosecution and as they turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, the other prosecution witnesses were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses.

Learned Sr.APP prayed that this court may issue summons to remaining witnesses, based on his submission perused the documents available on record and statement of victim who deposed herein in which it is clear that there is no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused no.1 to 4 .
Therefore, the PW-1 and 2 are the victim/injured to this case, they turned hostile for which issuance of summons to remaining witnesses no purpose will serve.
Therefore, submission made by the learned SPP is hereby rejected and remaining witnesses i.e, are ordered to be given up as it would no purpose summon them before the court.
Therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

However in this case no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused no.1 to 4 and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused no.1 to 4 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 C.C.4214/2019 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused no.1 to 4 ,
for which, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the 'Negative'.
13. Point No.5

: In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 4 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 4 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A,
504, 323 and 324 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 4 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 4 is ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
There is no order as to disposal of the properties in this case, since split up case is pending against accused no.5.
Keep the original file along with the split up C.C.9756/2022 pending against accused no.5.
(Judgment typed to my online dictation by the Stenographer, computerized copy revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 05th day of November 2025.)
(KESHAVA.K) XXXII

Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Bengaluru.
